local_execution.environment: isolated container, no HTTP, no browser, no production
local_execution.note: Committed source is an equivalent Node reproduction of the pinned JS interception; it is not the full original Python/Playwright browser test.

observations: After first resolved snapshot-A, interceptor stores one global lastBody promise.
Before second fetch resolves, wait predicate lastBody!==null is already true and lastBody yields snapshot-A rather than pending snapshot-B.
After second fetch resolves lastBody finally yields B; same stale-body mechanism reproduces for third request before C resolution.
The browser's fixed synthetic digest could mask a repeated-body false positive; no actual browser failure is proven by this isolated reproduction.

owner_boundary.scope: QA owner handoff; do not edit CI-only owner workflow, source, product-dev or main

proposed_owner_freshness_contract: For every read action record expected next request sequence, then associate cloned body with the same request URL/id (monotonic queue, or per-request key).
Wait for exact fresh response sequence and its fulfilled clone body before assertion; a globally non-null prior Promise must not satisfy a later read.
Verify 3 distinct response bodies are bound to 3 distinct browser fetches, preserve original request count, HTTP status/Cache-Control, digest, TTL, same-document and external-request-deny checks.
Do not mock API/fulfill routes or infer original U3 byte-exact PASS from compatible CI.
rollback: This governance-only evidence may be reverted; PR#4 owner change requires independent review.
